title: Maryland PSC Order No. 92537 (Case No. 9715)

BEFORE THE 
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 
OF MARYLAND 
Case No. 9715 
Issue Date: July 22, 2026 
ORDER ON JOINT MARYLAND EXELON UTILITIES’ REQUEST FOR 
RECONSIDERATION OF REQUEST TO TRACK INCREMENTAL PROJECT 
DEVELOPMENT COSTS 
On April 8, 2026, the Commission issued Order No. 92281,1 which authorized 
Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (“BGE”), Potomac Electric Power Company (“Pepco”), 
and Delmarva Power & Light Company (“Delmarva Power”) (collectively “the Joint Maryland 
Exelon Utilities” or “JMEUs”) to issue requests for proposals (“RFPs”) for their energy storage 
plans subject to certain conditions and modifications. As part of Order No. 92281, the 
Commission chose to defer any decisions on cost recovery for BGE and Pepco Holdings Inc. 
(“PHI”)2 pending discussion of bill impacts at utility pre-award confidential conferences as 
discussed in the order. 
On May 11, 2026, the JMEUs issued a request3 for expedited approval to defer early-
stage development costs of a combined $2.5 million for Commission-approved battery storage 
programs into a regulatory asset to be reviewed for prudency in future rate cases. On June 9, 
2026, the Commission issued Order No. 92467, which denied the JMEU’s request for approval

the Next Generation Energy Act, Maryland Energy Storage Program, Case No. 9715. 
2 PHI’s Maryland utilities are Pepco and Delmarva Power.

for a modification of Order No. 92281 to defer early-stage development costs into a regulatory 
asset.4 
On July 9, 2026, the JMEUs filed a request5 for reconsideration of Order No. 92467. 
For the reasons described herein, the Commission conditionally approves the JMEU request. 
The JMEU Request 
The JMEUs’ request is largely an expansion of their arguments made in their first 
request. The JMEUs request authorization to track incremental project development costs up 
to the amounts identified in their original filing as a regulatory asset. The JMEUs state that 
they “are supportive of clear guardrails, including treatment of the proposed amounts as a 
ceiling, as recommended by OPC, and Staff’s recommendations to separately track costs by 
utility and program, and to distinguish among internal resources, external costs, and 
materials.”6 
The JMEUs state that their request is “limited to establishing a tracking mechanism for 
pre-award development costs” and that the “mechanism would support the targeted 
development work and resources needed to vet projects and partners identified through the 
RFP process, refine proposed locations, costs, and schedules, and develop accurate bill impact 
analyses for the Commission’s confidential pre-award conferences.”7 The JMEUs state that the 
requested tracking mechanism would facilitate the pre-award development activities necessary 
to produce better-informed proposals and improve the likelihood of successful project 
outcomes.

The JMEUs further state that they “are not seeking a determination regarding cost 
recovery, prudency, amortization, or return at this stage of the proceeding. Rather, the request 
is limited to authorization to track associated development costs in a regulatory asset pending 
future Commission review.”8 The JMEUs clarify that the Commission “would retain, as it 
always has, the ability to determine whether such costs were prudently incurred, whether 
recovery is appropriate, the period over which any recovery should occur, and whether any 
return should be authorized.”9 The JMEUs also state that “the request does not guarantee 
recovery of those costs and does not seek a determination regarding prudency, amortization, 
or return. Instead, it preserves the JMEUs’ ability to present such costs in a future proceeding, 
while maintaining the Commission’s full discretion to determine whether the costs were 
prudently incurred, whether recovery is appropriate, the manner of recovery, and whether any 
return should be authorized.”10 
The JMEUs also state that the request is consistent with Commission practice allowing 
regulatory asset treatment for incremental development costs associated with new utility 
programs, such as the networked geothermal pilot.11 
Finally, the JMEUs indicate that consistent with Order No. 92467, the JMEUs will 
continue to move forward with implementation of the Next Generation Energy Act (“NGEA”) 
relating to the Maryland Energy Storage Program, including issuance of the approved RFPs. 
However, absent authorization to track incremental development costs, the JMEUs “will 
necessarily limit pre-award development activities to those that can be supported using 
currently available resources.”12 As a result, the JMEUs indicate that the information presented

during the confidential pre-award conferences “may reflect broader cost ranges, less developed

Commission Decision 
Although the JMEUs cite the Commission's approval of regulatory asset treatment for 
incremental development costs associated with new utility programs in the networked 
geothermal pilot as precedent, this is not a perfectly apt comparison because the WARMTH 
Act (“Act”)14 allowed the utilities to request a regulatory asset for the work of developing the 
pilot program proposals, and also allowed the Commission to grant approval of a regulatory 
asset if it found the proposed plan and costs were necessary to meet the requirements of the 
Act. Finally, the Act gave the Commission final authority to allow recovery or not in a rate 
case. 
In the WARMTH Act proceeding, the Commission directed BGE15 in Order No. 
9139016 to file detailed plans and budgets for how it would develop the networked geothermal 
pilots. After receipt of the detailed plans and budgets, in Order No. 91460,17 the Commission 
granted conditional approval of a regulatory asset to BGE. To gain final approval, BGE was 
required to show more detailed information about its progress. Finally, after receiving the 
detailed information, the Commission granted BGE’s regulatory asset in Order No. 91538.18

5 
The Commission found that BGE had addressed all the areas for which additional information 
was sought; therefore, the Commission removed the conditional status of the regulatory asset. 
To the Commission’s knowledge, no JMEU has issued an RFP to-date for its 
distribution-connected energy storage programs despite Commission approval to issue RFPs 
issued April 8, 2026 in Order No. 92281. By comparison, The Potomac Edison Company 
(“PE”) provided notice on May 28, 2026 to the Commission that it had issued its RFP. The 
Commission reminds the JMEUs that the NGEA includes operational deadlines with the 
deadline for the first round of procurements being November 1, 2027. The Commission is 
concerned that the JMEUs are not developing their programs and related RFPs in a sufficient 
manner to meet the NGEA deadlines as compared to PE. 
Therefore, similar to the network geothermal pilot, the Commission will approve a 
regulatory asset, but subject to certain conditions. These conditions will be imposed to 
incentivize the JMEUs to move more rapidly to implement their NGEA requirements in 
addition to providing analyses of sufficient quality and detail to facilitate productive 
confidential pre-award conferences. Specifically, the Commission expects that the JMEUs will 
now be able to apply sufficient resources to forestall the purported consequences of not being 
approved for a regulatory asset, cited as broader cost ranges, less developed project-specific 
information, less extensive engineering and outreach review, and less refined assessments of 
project execution risk in their analyses. 
The Commission also accepts the JMEUs’ offer to implement guardrails including 
treatment of the proposed development cost amounts as a ceiling, as recommended by OPC, 
and Staff’s recommendations to separately track costs by utility and program, and to 
distinguish among internal resources, external costs, and materials. The conditional status of 

6 
the regulatory asset shall be removed after the pre-award conferences once the JMEUs 
successfully demonstrate that all of the conditions described herein are met. 
IT IS, THEREFORE, this 22nd day of July, in the year of Two Thousand Twenty-Six, 
by the Public Service Commission of Maryland, ORDERED: 
(1) 
that the Joint Maryland Exelon Utilities’ request for approval for a regulatory 
asset for program development costs to implement their statutory requirements under the Next 
Generation Energy Act is hereby Conditionally Approved subject to the following 
requirements to remove the conditional status: 
(a) 
the JMEUs shall issue RFPs for their distribution connected energy 
storage programs required by Order No. 92281 within 30 days of the 
issuance of this Order; 
(b) 
the JMEUs shall prepare analyses of sufficient quality and detail to 
facilitate productive confidential pre-award conferences to fully meet 
the requirements of Order No. 92281 in addition to forestalling the 
JMEU’s purported consequences of not being approved for a 
regulatory asset as described herein; and 
(c) 
the JMEUs shall cap their program development costs in the regulatory 
asset and provide tracking of program costs and resources as described 
herein.
